ns2:section.sectionText: This section is for Undergraduates. Lectures and assignments will be completed online. Class will meet bi-weekly for a synchronous "live" session via Zoom involving discussion and teamwork. For students unable to attend synchronous "live" sessions, alternative assignments will be offered. The course examines the interaction of social psychology and law. Topics include biases in legal decision-making, employment discrimination and discriminatory intent, affirmative action and diversity, rape victim blaming, race and police conduct, eyewitness identification and memory, false confessions and lie detection, race and jury decision-making, and social perception. **Elective course for Cognitive, Diversity, Intradisciplinary, Personality, or Social Psychology Concentration**"
